name: rembrandt-tech-painter
title: Rembrandt-style modern-tech book art
summary: Paint a chapter/cover image of modern tech (servers, cloud, MCP, computers) in the locked Rembrandt house style and get it into the Leanpub manuscript.
reference_note: Public domain: Rembrandt died in 1669, so every painting and its museum release is out of copyright. The set is fixed and versioned so a whole book keeps one visual identity instead of each generation reinterpreting the style from a prompt.
body:
Paint a book illustration in the fixed Rembrandt house style for a modern-tech subject.

1. Read the chapter and pick one concrete image moment: a server rack hums in a dark room at night, the many hands of one cloud reach out as a guild, the two instruments of an MCP handshake meet across a desk by candlelight, a single computer glows in a corner study. One scene per image; a subject paragraph is a list you can turn into a scene, not a scene itself.
2. Keep the style lock constant; it comes from the reference set, not from your prose. The locked set is the three public-domain Rembrandt plates the painter is configured with (The Night Watch, the Drapers Guild, a self portrait): Rembrandt died in 1669, so every one is public domain and safe to condition a whole book on.
3. Write the prompt about the subject only: what is in the frame, what is happening, where the single shaft of light falls. Do not apologise to the painter, do not pile on style adjectives that fight the conditioning, and never name the real machines or secrets involved.
4. Call paint_image with that prompt, the slug set to the chapter slug plus a short image tag, the manuscript_images_dir set to the book manuscript images folder, and seed 0 for a fresh random composition.
5. Curate by hand. The painter returns two files and no judgement, and vision is off, so you must not accept an image you have not opened. Look, keep or discard; when a composition misses, regenerate the same slug with one fixed seed or a lower strength until one lands.
6. Reference the kept file from the chapter Markua by relative path in the manuscript tree so Leanpub finds it.
7. Before the image counts as done, run the Leanpub preview build: merge, POST the preview, poll the job status, and check the returned pdf and epub preview URLs, exactly as ADR 0001 of the Book Drafting Pipeline sets for every rendered image. A painting has more to go wrong at print than a diagram, so this gate matters more here, not less.
8. When a style drifts away from the house look, record it as a follow-on task rather than quietly changing the locked reference set: the set is fixed and versioned on purpose.
